topic.title: Strategic Learning and Incentive Design
topic.overview: Learning systems interact with people or organizations that may change behavior in response to their rules. This topic studies strategic classification, collaborative learning, mechanism design, and information design. Instead of treating manipulation as arbitrary noise, the models examine what rational participants gain from reporting, withholding, or changing information.
topic.whyItMatters: An accurate predictor can create incentives that undermine its own data or intended policy. Designing rewards and communication rules jointly with learning can make honest participation compatible with good outcomes.
topic.evolution: Earlier examples involve economic decisions and online mechanisms. Recent work analyzes strategic responses to fairness interventions and competitive collaboration, including mechanisms that restore honest updates. The newest representatives extend incentive questions to policy allocation and natural-language persuasion, while uncertainty about participant costs complicates robust strategic classification.
openQuestions: How can incentive guarantees remain useful when participants’ costs and objectives are only partly known?
Which learning improvements persist after people adapt to the deployed system?

papers.tldr: The paper develops a theoretical framework for acquiring and pricing training data when limited computation prevents exact valuation.

papers.title: Ambiguous Strategic Classification
papers.tldr: The paper models partial classifier disclosure as a learnable choice and develops algorithms for strategic classification under that ambiguity.

papers.title: Approximate Proportionality in Online Fair Division
papers.tldr: Online PROP1 fairness admits useful approximation guarantees under non-adaptive arrivals or maximum-item-value predictions, despite failures of natural greedy rules.

papers.title: Beyond Rational Illusion: Behaviorally Realistic Strategic Classification
papers.tldr: Pro-SF incorporates prospect-theory mechanisms into strategic classification to account for psychologically biased responses to classifiers.

papers.title: CoopEval: Benchmarking Cooperation-Sustaining Mechanisms and LLM Agents in Social Dilemmas
papers.tldr: CoopEval finds that contracts and mediation best support cooperation among the tested capable LLM agents in social dilemmas.

papers.title: Curated Synthetic Data Doesn’t Have to Collapse: A Theoretical Study of Generative Retraining with Pluralistic Preferences
papers.tldr: Under certain conditions, curating synthetic outputs with multiple reward functions yields stable, diverse retraining dynamics with a weighted Nash bargaining interpretation.

papers.title: Desirable Effort Fairness and Optimality Trade-offs in Strategic Learning
papers.tldr: The paper formalizes how encouraging desirable changes fairly can trade off against a strategic classifier’s predictive objective.

papers.title: Incentivizing Truthfulness and Collaborative Fairness in Bayesian Learning
papers.tldr: A Bayesian data-reward mechanism combines fairness with equilibrium incentives for truthful contributions under stated conditions.

papers.title: Is Your LLM Overcharging You? Tokenization, Transparency, and Incentives
papers.tldr: The paper identifies incentives for token-count misreporting and derives character-proportional token pricing as necessary to remove them in its framework.

papers.title: Keep Everyone Happy: Online Fair Division of Numerous Items with Few Copies
papers.tldr: Feature-based contextual bandit algorithms support online fair allocation when there are many distinct items but few repeated observations of each.

papers.title: Knowing Who, Not How Much: Learning-Augmented Mechanisms for Consumer Utility Maximization
papers.tldr: Predicting the highest-valued agent’s identity enables a truthful online mechanism with distinct consistency and robustness guarantees for consumer utility.

papers.title: Leaderboard Incentives: Model Rankings under Strategic Post-Training
papers.tldr: A game-theoretic analysis shows that tune-before-test can, under mild conditions, align strategic model competition with latent-quality rankings.

papers.title: Learning Unanimously Acceptable Lotteries via Queries
papers.tldr: Query-based algorithms find unanimously acceptable lotteries or certify infeasibility, using adaptivity, randomization, and advice to reduce stakeholder elicitation costs.

papers.title: Multi-Level Strategic Classification: Incentivizing Improvement through Promotion and Relegation Dynamics
papers.tldr: The paper shows how promotion and relegation thresholds can incentivize honest improvement, enabling arbitrarily high advancement under stated model conditions.

papers.title: NBCG: Nash-Bargained Causal Game for Long-Tailed Multi-Label NLP
papers.tldr: NBCG organizes labels into learned dependency-based coalitions and uses Nash bargaining to prioritize underserved groups during training.

papers.title: Off-Policy Evaluation with Strategic Agents via Local Disclosure
papers.tldr: Local policy explanations reveal information about strategic responses, enabling a policy-value estimator with consistency under a conditional log-normal cost-sensitivity assumption.

papers.title: On the Fragility of Data Attribution When Learning Is Distributed
papers.tldr: A distributed-learning participant can inflate its measured data contribution with synthetic batches while preserving model accuracy.

papers.title: Online Contract Design With Unknown Technology
papers.tldr: Knowing a candidate set of agent actions can remove exponential problem-size dependence in online contract learning despite unknown action availability.

papers.title: Optimal Pricing for Data-Augmented AutoML Marketplaces
papers.tldr: The proposed AutoML marketplace prices data-augmented models by their performance improvements and offers options for differing buyer valuations.

papers.title: Overcoming the Incentive Collapse Paradox
papers.tldr: Sentinel auditing sustains human effort at finite cost in the studied delegation model and improves budget allocation for statistical inference.

papers.title: Personalized Policy Learning through Discrete Experimentation
papers.tldr: DLPT learns personalized continuous policies from discrete randomized experiments and improves creator-incentive optimization in a platform application.

papers.title: Position: Enabling Fair Revenue Sharing for Data Providers in GenAI Systems
Position: GenAI Systems Should Implement Contribution-Aware Revenue Sharing for Data Providers
papers.tldr: The authors propose compensating data providers according to measurable contributions to generated outputs through scalable attribution and revenue-sharing systems.

papers.title: Position: Infringement cannot be cured after training
papers.tldr: The paper argues that post-training changes cannot retroactively resolve liability from unlawful data acquisition and ingestion.

papers.title: Position: Machine Learning for Heart Transplant Allocation Policy Optimization Should Account for Incentives
papers.tldr: The authors argue that heart transplant allocation policies must account for participants’ incentives and strategic behavior.

papers.title: Robust Strategic Classification under Decision-Dependent Cost Uncertainty
papers.tldr: A two-stage robust framework models how classifier decisions change future manipulation costs and can help curb strategic gaming over time.

papers.title: Verbalized Bayesian Persuasion
papers.tldr: A verbalized Bayesian persuasion framework combines LLM dialogue with a game solver to study strategic information sharing in natural-language scenarios.
